stem: For x>0, prove log_2(32x^3)=5+3log_2 x, then solve log_2(sqrt(x))=log_2(32x^3)-8. [7]
questions.title: Logarithmic identities
solution: The product and power laws give 5+3log_2x. Put L=log_2x: L/2=5+3L-8=3L-3. Hence 5L/2=3, L=6/5 and x=2^(6/5).

stem: Events A,B satisfy P(A)=x, P(B)=1-x/2 and P(A union B)=7/8. Given independence, find all admissible x and P(A' intersect B'). [9]
questions.title: Independence with a parameter
solution: Independence gives P(A intersect B)=x(1-x/2). Also P(A union B)=x+1-x/2-x(1-x/2)=1+x^2/2-x/2=7/8. Hence 4x^2-4x+1=0, so (2x-1)^2=0 and x=1/2. Finally P(A' intersect B')=1-P(A union B)=1/8.

stem: The polynomial p(z)=z^3+z+10 has a root 1+2i.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Explain why 1-2i is also a root.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Factor p and find all roots.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Find the product of the moduli of the roots.

questions.title: Complex roots and factorization
solution: Real coefficients imply conjugate roots. (z-(1+2i))(z-(1-2i))=z^2-2z+5, and p=(z^2-2z+5)(z+2). Roots: 1+2i,1-2i,-2. Product of moduli=sqrt5(sqrt5)(2)=10.

stem: A quartic f satisfies f'(x)=4(x+2)(x-1)(x-3) and f(0)=5.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Expand and integrate to find f.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find and classify all stationary points.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Find the inflection points.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Find the tangent at x=0.

questions.title: Polynomial calculus
solution: Expand f'=4x^3-8x^2-20x+24. Hence f=x^4-(8/3)x^3-10x^2+24x+5. Stationary x=-2,1,3. Sign changes give minima at -2 and 3, maximum at 1. Values are f(-2)=-137/3, f(1)=52/3, f(3)=-4. f''=12x^2-16x-20=4(3x^2-4x-5), so x=(2+/-sqrt19)/3; substituting into f gives the two inflection points. At x=0, slope=24 and point (0,5), so tangent y=24x+5.

stem: For angles where expressions are defined:

parts.label: a
parts.html: prove cot(2x)=(cot x-tan x)/2.

parts.label: b
parts.html: solve cot(2x)=0 for 0<x<pi.

parts.label: c
parts.html: differentiate the identity to derive a relation involving csc^2(2x), csc^2x and sec^2x.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Evaluate integral_0^(pi/4) (csc^2x+sec^2x) dx as an improper expression and explain its divergence.

questions.title: Trigonometric proof and differentiation
solution: Using cos2x=cos^2x-sin^2x and sin2x=2sinx cosx gives the identity. cot2x=0 when cos2x=0, so x=pi/4,3pi/4. Differentiating: -2csc^2(2x)=(-csc^2x-sec^2x)/2, hence 4csc^2(2x)=csc^2x+sec^2x.
The antiderivative is -cotx+tanx. As x approaches 0+, cotx tends to infinity, so the improper integral diverges.

stem: A population P obeys dP/dt=0.3P(1-P/5000), P(0)=400.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find when P=2500.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Find the maximum growth rate and when it occurs.

parts.label: d
parts.html: State the long-term population.

questions.title: Differential equations and population
solution: Substitution verifies both the equation and P(0)=400. P=2500 gives 1+11.5e^(-0.3t)=2, so t=ln(11.5)/0.3=8.14. The quadratic 0.3P(1-P/5000) is maximal at P=2500, giving rate 375; this occurs at the same time. The limit is 5000.
